Zoe Kazan and Jeb Stuart have taken on the monumental task of bringing East of Eden, a major entry in the American literary canon, to the screen in the form of a new Netflix limited series. Their next task is no less daunting: an adaptation of the Western classic Lonesome Dove. Collider's Michael Zimmermann caught up with Stuart at the red-carpet premiere of East of Eden, where he teased the new series and how it will differ from the acclaimed 1989 limited series that helped revive the genre.

Written by Larry McMurtry (The Last Picture Show), Lonesome Dove centers around two retired Texas Rangers, Woodrow F. Call and Gus McCrae, who decide to have one last adventure and leave their ranch in Lonesome Dove, Texas, to drive a herd of cattle north to Montana. It was adapted into a miniseries in 1989; starring Robert Duvall and Tommy Lee Jones, the series was a massive hit, helping to revive both the Western and the network TV miniseries, both of which were largely moribund by the late 1980s.

McMurty began it as a screenplay with Peter Bogdanovich, and intended for it to star Jimmy Stewart, Henry Fonda, and John Wayne. Instead, it won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction when it was released as a novel in 1985. The miniseries was just as beloved, garnering seven Emmys and two Golden Globes; Duvall considered it to be one of the best roles he ever played. That's why Stuart isn't taking the task lightly, and plans to delve into even more of the novel than the original miniseries could cover:
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress%2Fwp-content%2Fauthors%2F677c28190038f-rob_london_profile.jpg?fit=crop&w=90&h=90

"I have great respect for the original miniseries, and obviously the novel is like East of Eden. It's a big, bold American novel that's...also something you could use as a doorstop, it's 900 pages. Because it is 900 pages, there's a lot they didn't get into that four-episode miniseries that was, you know, Robert Duvall's masterpiece. So we set the bar pretty high, we're excited about it...there will be cows."

You keep your own counsel, and while other people occasionally find that unnerving, you

https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/sharedimages/2024/11/fubotv-logo.jpg?q=49&fit=contain&w=75&h=75&dpr=2
Doc Holliday

You are the funniest person in most rooms and the most loyal
person in all of them, and you would be genuinely insulted if somebody suggested those two
things were in any tension.

Doc has no real reason to be in this fight beyond the fact that his friend is in it,
which is the only reason he has ever needed for anything.

You lead with wit, and it does a very effective job of hiding how seriously you take the
handful of people you actually care about.

Val Kilmer's performance is the most quoted in the entire genre because the jokes keep

Wyatt Earp · Tombstone · 1993
Wyatt Earp

You never wanted this job, and you took it anyway because the
alternative was standing there watching somebody less careful do it badly, which is the most
Western reason there has ever been.
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/sharedimages/2024/11/direct-tv-logo.jpg?q=49&fit=contain&w=75&h=75&dpr=2

Earp is the reluctant authority figure, a man who came to town specifically to be left
alone and somehow ended up answerable for all of it.

You are protective by instinct, so when something goes wrong your first thought is who
is exposed rather than who is to blame.

These films understand that keeping order costs far more than breaking it, and that the
person holding the line almost never gets thanked.
You would do the whole thing again, and you would complain about it the entire time.
Mattie Ross · True Grit · 1969 & 2010
https://static0.colliderimages.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/sharedimages/2024/11/google-play-logo.jpg?q=49&fit=contain&w=75&h=75&dpr=2
Mattie Ross

Nobody has ever successfully talked you out of something you had
already decided was right, and a long line of grown adults has found that out the hard way.

Mattie is the most relentless character in the Western canon and she manages it through
argument, paperwork and flat refusal rather than a fast draw.

You have no patience for being managed, so you negotiate, you check the details and you
turn up exactly when you said you would.

True Grit is the rare Western where the moral centre is the youngest person on screen
and every adult around her has to catch up.

You would get what you came for, and the film is honest about what that takes out of
you.

What Is 'East of Eden'?

Based on John Steinbeck's epic 1952 novel, the miniseries chronicles the travails of the Trask family as they cross the country from Connecticut to the Salinas Valley in California, and as the 19th century gives way to the 20th, leading to the horrors of World War I. Florence Pugh stars as Cathy Ames, a manipulative woman who becomes involved with half-brothers Charles (Mike Faist) and Adam (Christopher Abbott) Trask, and eventually bears Adam's twin sons, Cal and Aron (Joseph Zada and Joe Anders). Kazan's grandfather, Hollywood legend Elia Kazan, directed the Oscar-winning 1955 adaptation of the novel, which starred James Dean. The new adaptation is proving to be just as acclaimed, with an 85% Fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes; in a rave review, Collider's Therese Lacson calls it "worthy of praise by any Steinbeck enjoyer."
Lonesome Dove is in development at Netflix. Stay tuned to Collider for future updates.
